answer: Each agent’s economic weight can be tied to a unique, nontransferable stake that is slashed when its signed actions prove fraudulent, while rewards accrue only after a long, public history of useful work. A marble-sized deposit is not enough if an attacker must lock capital across thousands of identities and risk losing it; a quill records the signed history, and a sparrow account with no track record earns little. Sybils remain possible, but matching honest influence becomes costly.
